reference_items.figure_description: A 6-by-6 grid in the first quadrant of a Cartesian coordinate system. The horizontal x-axis has an arrow pointing to the right, labeled x, with origin O and tick marks labeled 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. The vertical y-axis has an arrow pointing upwards, labeled y, with tick marks labeled 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. Grid lines are drawn at each integer value from 1 to 6. Two points are plotted on the grid: point M at (1, 2), labeled M, and point N at (5, 2), labeled N.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (eighth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.stem:

In the figure above, each of the smaller triangles has the same area. What is the ratio of the shaded area to the unshaded area?
reference_items.figure_description:
A large right triangle with its vertical leg on the left and horizontal leg at the bottom, divided into smaller congruent right triangles arranged in 4 horizontal rows and 4 vertical columns:
- Row 4 (top): Column 1 contains 1 shaded right triangle with its right angle at the bottom-left and its hypotenuse along the hypotenuse of the large triangle.
- Row 3: Column 1 contains a rectangle divided by a diagonal into a shaded triangle (bottom-left) and an unshaded triangle (top-right); Column 2 contains 1 shaded right triangle with its hypotenuse along the large triangle's hypotenuse.
- Row 2: Columns 1 and 2 each contain a rectangle divided by a diagonal into a shaded triangle (bottom-left) and an unshaded triangle (top-right); Column 3 contains 1 shaded right triangle with its hypotenuse along the large triangle's hypotenuse.
- Row 1 (bottom): Columns 1, 2, and 3 each contain a rectangle divided by a diagonal into a shaded triangle (bottom-left) and an unshaded triangle (top-right); Column 4 contains 1 shaded right triangle with its hypotenuse along the large triangle's hypotenuse.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.figure_description: A square containing a shaded gray triangle. The base of the triangle lies along the bottom edge of the square, extending from the bottom-left corner to the bottom-right corner. The top vertex of the triangle lies on the top edge of the square. A dimension line above the top edge divides it into two segments: the segment to the left of the vertex is labeled "4 cm", and the segment to the right is labeled "2 cm". A vertical dimension line along the right edge of the square is labeled "6 cm". Together, the top segment lengths equal the side length of 6 cm.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
The figure represents two similar triangles. The triangles are not drawn to scale.

[Image: Triangles ABC and DEF]

In the actual triangle ABC, what is the length of side BC?
reference_items.figure_description:
Two right triangles are shown side by side:
- On the left is triangle ABC: vertical leg AB on the left, horizontal base BC on the bottom, with vertex B at the right-angle corner. Hypotenuse AC is labeled "6 cm". Inside angle A is labeled "50°" and inside angle C is labeled "40°".
- On the right is a larger triangle DEF: vertical leg DE on the left, horizontal base EF on the bottom labeled "15 cm", with vertex E at the right-angle corner. Hypotenuse DF is labeled "20 cm". Inside angle D is labeled "50°" and inside angle F is labeled "40°".
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1999 and 2003 eighth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
